subject: Approval request: pilot latency flexibility & onboarding credit for DataWave
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@datawave.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@datawave.ai, Rupal Sen <rupal.sen@datawave.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot SLO ask: short-term tail latency tolerance + onboarding credit

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the model performance in hosted mode looks really promising for our summarization pilot. Before we move to the pilot SOW, procurement has two asks we want to surface early so we can close the loop:

- Tail latency tolerance: for the first 60–90 days of pilot traffic (expected bursty patterns), we need a temporary P95 latency guardrail of 350ms instead of the standard 200ms in the standard SLA. We understand this is an exception and are open to an explicit sunset/metrics gating.
- One-time onboarding credit: given we are an early-stage customer and will do significant prompt engineering during pilot, we'd request a one-time onboarding credit to offset initial infra costs — ballpark $20–30k.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate a short-term tolerance and a one-time credit, and what approvals you would need? We plan to sign the SOW next week if we can get alignment. Attaching a draft SOW for reference (SOW includes the pilot scope and traffic profiles).

Attachments: DataWave_SOW_v1.pdf

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Product
DataWave.ai
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@datawave.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot SLO ask: short-term tail latency tolerance + onboarding credit

Thanks Liam — appreciate the clear asks and the SOW.

Marissa / Ben / Jonas — looping you in to start deal-desk and legal review. Quick summary: DataWave requests a temporary P95 latency tolerance increase to 350ms for a 60–90 day pilot window, plus a one-time onboarding credit in the $20–30k range. Pilot expected to start mid-December.

My proposal (to speed approvals):
- Conditional approval for transient SLO tolerance (P95 <= 350ms) for 90 days, with these controls:
  - Redwood will provide per-minute telemetry for the pilot and a weekly health check.
  - If P95 exceeds 450ms for two consecutive weeks, Redwood can revert to standard routing and the pilot may be paused.
- One-time onboarding credit: $25,000 applied as a first-invoice credit; finance signoff required.

I think this is commercially acceptable if Legal is comfortable with the addendum language. Requesting deal-desk + exec signoff on the above so we can return to DataWave w/ a tracked amendment.

Next steps: Marissa — can you run a quick cost impact & approve the $25k credit? Ben — can you review the SLA addendum draft? Jonas — need exec signoff if this looks reasonable.

Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot SLO ask: short-term tail latency tolerance + onboarding credit

Vanessa — I ran the numbers with finance. Notes below:

- Cost impact: $25,000 one-time credit reduces expected first-quarter ARR by ~2.1% for this deal size; pilot expected ACV if converted ~ $1.2M.
- Operational risk: 90-day P95 @ 350ms is feasible on hosted: we'll enable a dedicated lightweight routing policy and increase KV cache TTL to reduce tail. There's moderate risk if traffic spikes beyond the pilot profile.

I've uploaded a redline of the SOW + a draft SLA addendum with explicit sunset (90 days) and telemetry requirements. See attachments and HubSpot link below.

Attachments: DataWave_SLA_Addendum_draft.docx, DW_onboarding_cost_model.xlsx
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deals/DW-2026-118

Ben — please review the addendum language. If legal is okay, please mark APPROVE and Jonas can sign-off with a short exec note.

Marissa Cole
Senior Revenue Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot SLO ask: short-term tail latency tolerance + onboarding credit

Thanks team — I reviewed Marissa's cost summary and Ben's quick note (below). Approving the request with conditions.

Executive decision (approved):
- One-time onboarding credit: $25,000 to be applied as a first-invoice credit. Finance to record under promotional credits and update ARR forecast accordingly.
- Temporary SLO amendment: P95 latency tolerance relaxed to 350ms for a fixed 90-day pilot window, starting on the signed SOW effective date.

Conditions (must be included in the amendment):
1) Telemetry & reporting: Redwood provides minute-level P95/P99 telemetry and weekly health reports.
2) Sunset & rollback: Amendment expires automatically after 90 days unless both parties agree in writing to extend. If P95 > 450ms for two consecutive weekly reports, Redwood may suspend the pilot routing and provide remediation steps.
3) No SLA credits beyond the standard service credit policy — this is a controlled, temporary exception; commercial credits limited to the one-time onboarding credit stated above.

Ben/Marissa — proceed to finalize the SLA addendum with the above language. Ben, legal to greenlight and provide standard indemnity language. Marissa, once the doc is ready, send to DataWave and attach a DocuSign envelope. Vanessa — you can confirm with Liam and close the loop.

Jonas Weber
VP Sales | Redwood Inference
